metadata.title: Students’ 2018 PISA reading self-concept: Identifying predictors and examining model generalizability for emergent bilinguals

design_fields.q1_rationale: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variable is students’ reading self-concept rather than a cognitive achievement score for which PISA generates plausible values.
design_fields.q2_rationale: The study explicitly states that student sampling weights (scaled) were included in each analysis.
design_fields.q3_rationale: The study used multilevel modeling, which accounts for the clustering of students within schools.
design_fields.q4_rationale: The study does not mention any external validation strategies and only discusses internal validation methods.

design_fields.q4b_note: LLM (gpt-5.4-nano): “participants from the United States who participated in PISA 2018 served as the baseline group… We then utilized a multilevel modeling approach to test model generalizability… We disaggregated and compared findings for both emergent bilinguals and native English speakers.”
